description:
Abort semantics (port-map §4, §10.2).

OctoPi.Agent.AbortRef:
- new/0 → reference, creates ETS row
- abort/1 → sets the flag
- aborted?/1 → reads flag (read_concurrent ETS table owned by
  OctoPi.Agent.AbortRegistry GenServer)
- forget/1 → deletes row (called at session end)

Loop integration:
- Loop checks AbortRef.aborted?/1 between turns and before LLM stream.
- Tool handlers receive the abort_ref as third arg; they must check
  periodically OR pass it into Task.Supervisor.async_stream with an
  on_timeout.
- OctoPi.Agent.abort/1:
  1. Sets the ETS flag so cooperative checkers see it immediately.
  2. Task.shutdown(loop_task, :brutal_kill) for hard abort — tool
     tasks are linked so they die with it.
- Cleanup: session appends synthetic assistant message with
  stop_reason :aborted + errorMessage, emits agent_end, becomes idle.
  Queues are NOT cleared (ape TS).

TDD:
- abort between turns → loop exits with :aborted on next check
- abort during LLM stream → Producer's caller-dies path fires (from
  Phase 1 opi-hgb.2); loop translates to :aborted agent_end
- abort during tool exec → tool Task.shutdown kills it; loop emits
  tool_execution_end with cancelled flag, then agent_end
- double-abort is a no-op

Depends on z1d.3.
title: Cancellation: AbortRef (ETS flag) + Task.shutdown + graceful cleanup
